title: Prepositional 3: 'в' or 'на'?
description: The case form is the same after в and на. The choice depends on the noun's category. Drill the decision.
descriptionRussian: Форма падежа одинаковая после 'в' и 'на.' Выбор зависит от категории существительного.
intro: Here the difficulty stops being grammatical and starts being cultural. Both prepositions produce the identical ending, so nothing you learned in the last two lessons is at stake. What is at stake is which places Russian treats as somewhere you are inside and which as somewhere you are on top of. Some of those decisions will not match your intuition, and no rule derives them.
rules: The case form is the same after в and на. The CHOICE between them depends on the noun's category.
Use 'в' for buildings (магазин, офис, школа, театр), cities (Москва, Россия), and enclosed spaces (комната, квартира).
Use 'на' for surfaces (стол, диван, стул), events (концерт, урок, лекция), and idiomatic places (работа, улица, почта, стадион).

rows.label: Buildings
cells: в магазине, в офисе, в школе

rows.label: Idiomatic places
cells: на работе, на улице, на почте

items.promptEnglish: The book is on the table.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 2: which preposition do we use for surfaces?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 2: на is used for surfaces (на столе, на полу). Стол is a surface, so 'на.'

items.hint: Магазин is a building. Which preposition do buildings take?
items.explanation: Buildings take 'в' in Russian. Магазин is a building, so 'в магазине.' Compare with на работе (work is idiomatic на).

items.hint: Работа is one of the idiomatic 'на' places. Memorize it.
items.explanation: Russian says 'на работе' for 'at work,' not 'в работе.' Work is one of the idiomatic 'на' places, alongside улица, почта, стадион. These have to be memorized; they don't follow the building/event logic.
Cities and countries take 'в': в Москве, в России, в Америке. The same applies to all geographic place names ending in -а or a consonant.

items.hint: Концерт is an event. Which preposition?
items.explanation: Events take 'на': на концерте, на уроке, на лекции, на свадьбе. The Russian way of saying 'at an event' uses на rather than в.

items.hint: Офис is a building. Which preposition?
items.explanation: Офис is a building, so 'в офисе.' Note the contrast: 'на работе' (at work, idiomatic на) but 'в офисе' (at the office, building в). Russians can be at работа and офис simultaneously and use different prepositions.

blanks: Маша _____ библиотеке. (Masha is at the library.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Library is a building / enclosed space, so 'в библиотеке.'

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The children are at the stadium now.
errorCorrection.explanation: Стадион belongs to the set of event and activity places that take на, not в: на стадионе. Learners reach for в because стадион feels like a building, but Russian groups it with concerts and lessons (на концерте, на уроке). В стадионе is not used.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Mom is buying bread at the store.
errorCorrection.explanation: Магазин is a building, and buildings take в for location: в магазине. На магазине would place the action on top of the store's roof. The в/на split sends enclosed places and buildings (магазин, офис, школа) to в, and surfaces and event places (стол, работа, стадион) to на.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The plate is on the table.
errorCorrection.explanation: Стол is a surface, and surfaces take на for location: на столе. В столе means inside the table, as in a drawer, which is a different meaning. Russian reserves в for enclosed spaces and на for surfaces and event places.

minimalPairs.explanation: Russian uses 'на работе' for 'at work,' not 'в работе.' Work is one of the idiomatic 'на' places, alongside улица, почта, стадион.
Concerts and other events take 'на': на концерте, на лекции, на свадьбе. 'В концерте' is wrong; only 'на концерте' is standard.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort these locations by which preposition Russian uses.

reviewVocab.example: Выбор между 'в' и 'на' зависит от существительного.
